b1.text: Return to Zero (RZ) The RZ code is a further development of the NRZ code (Non-Return-to-Zero), in which the two-level values are equivalent to the binary value of the digit to be transmitted. The disadvantage of the NRZ code is that there are no level changes when transmitting a longer series of zeros or a set of ones. As a result, it is not possible for the receiver to recover the clock from the signal during this period. When transmitting a logical 1 with the level +1, the RZ code returns to level 0
